- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in early days of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., 75+ values) — model peaks too high and then drops too fast.
- Underestimates in late forecast days (last 5–10 days) — shows mean reversion bias, failing to capture sustained downward trends.
- Forecast lags behind true price movements — especially in downward trends, model delays the drop.
- Overconfident in short-term momentum — fails to account for volatility decay or policy-induced corrections.
- Sensitive to recent history — if last 5–10 days are high, model overweights that trend and fails to adjust for upcoming policy or supply shocks.
- Underestimates downward corrections after high peaks — model doesn’t fully account for regulatory or market correction mechanisms.
- Tends to smooth out volatility — underestimates sharp drops or spikes in true outcomes, especially in 30-day horizon.
